question: How do you structure a 45-minute GenAI system-design interview answer?
idealAnswerCore: Clarify the job-to-be-done, constraints (latency, cost, risk, tenancy), then walk ingestion → context/tools → model routing → guardrails → evals → serving/ops — call out 2–3 hard tradeoffs instead of naming every vendor.
idealAnswerFraming: Same as distributed-systems design: requirements first. Interviewers fail people who jump to 'we'll use LangChain'.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Ask: QPS, P95, data sensitivity, write actions, languages
Draw trust boundaries (user, docs, tools, model provider)
Pick an MVP path and a scale path
Define evals and kill switches as part of the design, not an afterthought
Quantify: tokens, index size, $ per day at 1k DAU
idealAnswerFollowups: What question do you ask first if the prompt is 'build ChatGPT for our company'?
How do you handle a interviewer who wants Kubernetes before the eval plan?

question: Design an internal knowledge assistant for 20k employees over Confluence, Slack, and Drive.
idealAnswerCore: ACL-aware connectors, incremental index, hybrid search + rerank, citation UX, per-app identity, evals on real tickets, and no write tools in v1 — retrieval isolation is the design, not the choice of GPT vs Claude.
idealAnswerFraming: Enterprise RAG system design. Spend time on permissions and freshness.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Auth: SSO; retrieval must filter by the user's tokens, not the bot's god mode
Connectors: webhooks/cursors for updates; tombstones on delete
Slack is noisy — channel allowlists and recency
Answer with links to the source page/message
Launch: one division canary, DLP, audit logs
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you index a Google Doc the user cannot open?
How fresh is 'good enough' for HR policy vs chat trivia?

question: Design a customer-support agent that can look up orders and issue refunds.
idealAnswerCore: Split chat from side effects: retrieve policy + order tools under the user's identity, draft replies with citations, and require a policy engine plus HITL or strict limits on refunds — evals must include adversarial tickets and idempotent refunds.
idealAnswerFraming: This is the classic agent design. Safety of money > fluency.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: v1: retrieve + draft for humans; v2: auto-refund under $X
Tools: get_order, list_payments, create_refund with idempotency keys
Policy as code, not only in the prompt
Injection: ticket text is untrusted
Metrics: containment, refund accuracy, handle time, CSAT
idealAnswerFollowups: What if the LLM is down during a sale?
How do you stop double refunds on retry?

question: Design a coding copilot for a 50-million-line monorepo.
idealAnswerCore: IDE client + context assembler (open files, grep, semantic retrieve, build errors), repo index with incremental updates, fill-in-the-middle plus chat/agent modes, secret scanning, and evals on private golden patches — do not stream the whole repo to a public model without a contract.
idealAnswerFraming: Staff-level. Mention privacy, latency for FIM, and agent vs autocomplete.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Autocomplete: <100ms local or small model; chat can be slower
Index: embeddings + symbols + build graph; sharded by repo path
Zero-retention or self-host for sensitive code
Agent mode: patch + tests in a sandbox, step budget
Eval: acceptance rate, SWE-like tasks on internal issues
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you keep the index fresh after every merge?
Would you run the agent on CI or only in the IDE?

question: Design a document-QA product for messy PDFs (scans, tables, slides).
idealAnswerCore: Parse with a layout-aware pipeline (OCR, tables, figures), store page/bbox metadata, retrieve with text + visual embeddings if needed, answer with page-level citations, and eval on table numbers — naive text extraction will fail the demo.
idealAnswerFraming: Multimodal RAG design without boiling the ocean.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Detect scanned vs digital PDFs
Keep table structure (HTML/markdown) not flattened soup
Citation: page + highlight coordinates
Queue big files as jobs; stream status
Human review for extracted amounts in finance
idealAnswerFollowups: When do you use a VLM over the page image vs OCR text?
How do you handle 500-page contracts?

question: Design a real-time voice agent for phone support (STT → LLM → TTS).
idealAnswerCore: Optimize for time-to-first-audio: streaming STT, speculative LLM, streaming TTS, interruption (barge-in), and a tight tool set — use a fast model for turn-taking and escalate to a reasoner only off the call path.
idealAnswerFraming: Latency budget in milliseconds. Mention WebRTC/SIP, not just the LLM.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Budget: STT partials <300ms, LLM first audio <800ms if possible
Endpointing and barge-in so the bot does not talk over the user
State machine for IVR-like flows plus LLM for the tail
PII: voice recordings have retention rules
Fallback to human queue with the transcript
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you handle an accent the STT mangles?
Where does tool calling sit without killing latency?

question: Design model routing for a SaaS feature that must hit a cost target and a quality bar.
idealAnswerCore: Classify intent/complexity, send easy traffic to small/cheap models, hard or failing cases to a frontier or reasoner, cache semantic hits, and keep an eval scorecard per route — never a single default 'best model'.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Signals: length, intent, user plan, validator fail, tenant SLO
Shadow the expensive model to label the router
Pin versions; a silent model upgrade is a routing bug
Per-route SLOs and $ dashboards
Safety route cannot skip guardrails to save money
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you train the complexity classifier without leaking PII?
What if the cheap model is fluent but unfaithful?

question: Design a multi-tenant LLM gateway used by many internal product teams.
idealAnswerCore: Centralize keys, quotas, tracing, retries, DLP, and model pinning behind an internal API with chargeback; give teams a prompt registry and eval hooks — the gateway is a control plane, not a place to hide business logic.
idealAnswerFraming: Platform design. Noisy neighbors and governance.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: AuthN/Z per team and environment
Token budgets and bulkheads (interactive vs batch vs evals)
Standard error model and streaming
Policy plugins: PII, allowlisted models
SLOs of the gateway vs the provider
idealAnswerFollowups: When may a team bypass the gateway?
How do you onboard a new provider without breaking teams?

question: Design an evaluation and launch plan for a GenAI feature that has no single gold answer.
idealAnswerCore: Write a rubric, build a 50–200 case golden set from real traces, add contract tests (schema, citations, refusals), LLM-as-judge calibrated to humans, then shadow → canary with online task metrics and a kill switch.
idealAnswerFraming: System design of quality. Interviewees who only say 'we'll A/B CSAT' are incomplete.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Contracts before judges
Slice by language and risk
Human panel monthly to recailbrate
Launch criteria written with PM/legal
Budget for eval spend in COGS
idealAnswerFollowups: What if judges disagree with support agents?
How small a canary is ethical for refunds?

question: Design a text-to-SQL assistant over a 3k-table warehouse without letting it DROP TABLE.
idealAnswerCore: Retrieve relevant schemas and certified metrics, generate SQL under a read-only role, dry-run EXPLAIN, lint for forbidden statements, and require warehouse row-level security — the model never sees admin credentials.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Don't paste 3k CREATE TABLEs; retrieve by question embedding + usage stats
Semantic layer / dbt metrics for business definitions
Allowlist: SELECT only; timeout; max bytes
Show the SQL and a sample before auto-run for destructive-looking queries
Eval: execution accuracy on a warehouse clone
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you handle ambiguous 'revenue' definitions?
What if the generated SQL is correct but scans 40TB?

question: Design an image-generation feature (ads, product shots) with brand and safety constraints.
idealAnswerCore: Separate prompt construction, a gated model API, content moderation on prompt and image, brand style LoRAs or IP-adapters, human review for external campaigns, and provenance (C2PA) — plus a policy for training-data/IP risk.
idealAnswerFraming: GenAI is not only LLMs. Show safety + brand.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Prompt templates with locked negative constraints
Moderation before and after generation
Do not fine-tune on unlicensed artist styles if legal forbids it
Cache and reuse approved assets
Eval: brand-guideline rubric + NSFW classifier false-positive rate
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you stop a user from generating a competitor's logo?
When is a human designer still in the loop?

question: Design for provider outage: your product is an LLM wrapper with 99.9% availability target.
idealAnswerCore: Multi-provider adapters with a tested degraded prompt, caches, circuit breakers, and a documented quality cliff — 99.9% is an error-budget conversation because model APIs will miss that alone.
idealAnswerFraming: Reliability system design. Be honest about vendor SLAs.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Primary + secondary + cache + retrieval-only mode
Prompt portability evals on the backup model
Shed batch before interactive
Status page and in-app banner
Error budget: freeze launches when burned
idealAnswerFollowups: Do you fail open to a weaker-aligned model?
How do you keep conversations consistent across failover?

question: How would you estimate cost and GPU/API capacity before building a GenAI feature?
idealAnswerCore: Start from DAU × messages × tokens × price (or GPU hours), add RAG embeddings and retries/evals (often 10–30% extra), then apply cache hit and routing discounts — present a range, not a fake-precise number.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Split input vs output tokens; output often dominates chat
Include failed retries and tool loops
Self-host: MFU, KV cache, replicas for P95, not just model weights
Sensitivity: ±2× tokens if history grows
Compare COGS to willingness-to-pay or hours saved
idealAnswerFollowups: Walk through 10k DAU support bot numbers out loud
When does self-hosting beat APIs?

question: Design a feedback flywheel that improves the product without poisoning the model.
idealAnswerCore: Collect implicit/explicit feedback with traces, cluster failures, promote to golden evals and retrieval/prompt fixes first; only then consider SFT on redacted, licensed, high-agreement data — thumbs-up is not a training label.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Privacy: redact before any vendor fine-tune
Human review on a sample of 'good' traces — they contain PII and bad advice
Prompt/RAG fixes are faster than weights
Watch distribution shift if you only train on happy users
Legal: user content license in ToS
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you avoid training on jailbreak 'successes'?
When is RL from production traces justified?

question: Design an on-device + cloud hybrid assistant (phone/laptop) that works offline.
idealAnswerCore: Run a quantized SLM locally for autocomplete, classification, and private drafts; escalate to cloud for hard tasks when online; keep a sync protocol for memory with encryption — never assume the local model is as aligned as the cloud policy stack.
idealAnswerFraming: Edge + privacy. Mention llama.cpp/MLX/NNAPI class runtimes without being vendor-religious.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Task router: local vs cloud based on sensitivity and hardness
On-device RAG over user files with local embeddings
Update path for model weights (signed, staged)
Offline UX: queue cloud jobs
Security: local tools still need sandboxing
idealAnswerFollowups: How do you eval a 7B local model vs cloud on the same rubric?
What if the user is on a 4GB RAM device?
